To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the pattern of recurrence changes in patients with noninvasive bladder cancer during the past two decades.
the pattern of recurrence in noninvasive papillary tumors changes during the course of the disease and that the pattern of progression is similar in the first and second decades of follow-up.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of the patterns of recurrent noninvasive bladder tumor, observed over a period of 2 decades, and with the evaluation of the prognostic significance of these patterns.
the study of the pattern of recurrence in bladder cancer patients treated with intravesical bacillus Calmette-Guerin (BCG) and the identification of prognostic factors.
the study of the effect of a magnetic field on the rate of growth of tumor cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the incidence of bladder cancer has increased in recent decades, with an increase in the number of new cases and deaths.
the use of the term “benign prostatic hypertrophy (BPH)” is inappropriate and that it is better to speak of “benign prostatitis” or “benign prostate disease” (BPD).

there are no data that would support a change in the current guidelines for the management of noninvasive bladder cancer, and that there is no need for change in the management of non-invasive bladder cancer at this time.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the expression of a few miRNAs in the serum is a potential biomarker for the diagnosis of bladder cancer.
the incidence of recurrence in patients with low-risk, noninvasive bladder cancer is significantly less than previously reported.
this study demonstrates a change in the pattern of recurrence of noninvasive bladder tumor during 2 decades in the same population of patients.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the current approach to treating nonmuscle-invasive bladder cancer is not working.

we need to be more careful when interpreting the results of our experiments.
